reflexive.condition: For every x in M, xRx.

symmetric.condition: For every x,y in M, xRy implies yRx.

transitive.condition: For every x,y,z in M, xRy and yRz imply xRz.

equivalence.condition: Reflexive AND symmetric AND transitive on the stated carrier.
equivalence.status: Explicit standard convention; no separate equivalence-definition paragraph was supplied.

conventions.statement: Use all relevant Euclidean geometric objects, not an invented subset. A segment is an unordered geometric point set. Polygons have a well-defined ordinary area.
conventions.impact: The positive scalar-equality relations need only well-defined length/area. The fixed-center negative example needs an ordinary noncentered segment.

conventions.statement: 447(2) uses one given O for all pairs and S_O(p)=2O-p. On segment sets S_O is an involution.
conventions.impact: Do not replace the relation by equal length or let O vary. Self-related centered segments exist; noncentered segments refute universal reflexivity.
Reflexivity is true under the first reading and false under the second. Symmetry is true, transitivity false and equivalence false under both.

conventions.statement: 449 requires both coplanarity and no common point, exactly as the student's quoted definition states.
conventions.impact: Coincident lines are not related. Equal variables remain permitted in property tests. No coincidence-inclusive parallel convention is substituted.

source_reviews.task: Determine whether congruence on the set of segments is an equivalence relation.
source_reviews.independent_solution: Each segment has its own length. Equality of length is reversible, and length(s)=length(t), length(t)=length(u) imply length(s)=length(u). Hence all three defining properties hold.

property_evidence.equivalence: The relation is reflexive, symmetric and transitive on the specified carrier.

examples.calculation: All three lengths are 2; sRt, tRu and sRu. Different positions and directions do not prevent segment congruence.
Lengths 2 and 3 differ, so not sRv. An equivalence relation need not relate every pair.

source_reviews.equivalence_classes: All segments of a fixed length.
source_tasks_solved: justification by the three supplied properties

source_reviews.task: For each of the three given relations, decide reflexivity, symmetry, transitivity and equivalence.

subrelations.independent_solution: Area is a scalar function of a polygon. Equality of that scalar is reflexive, symmetric and transitive, irrespective of shape or congruence.

examples.calculation: 2*3=1*6=(4*3)/2=6. Adjacent area equalities imply the first and third polygons have equal area, although their shapes differ.
Its area is 1, not 6, so it is not related to the preceding polygons.

subrelations.carrier: All Euclidean segments, with a single fixed center O.
subrelations.independent_solution: S_O is an involution. Symmetry follows by applying it twice. A noncentered segment is not fixed, so universal reflexivity fails. For that x, let y=S_O(x) and z=x. Both premises xRy and yRz hold, but the conclusion xRx fails. Centered segments are self-related, so this is not an irreflexive relation either.

property_evidence.transitive: For the nonfixed x above, y=S_O(x), z=x give xRy and yRz but not xRz.
property_evidence.equivalence: Reflexivity and transitivity fail on the whole segment carrier.

self_relation_example.calculation: S_O(h)=h. A nondegenerate segment is fixed exactly when its midpoint is O.

subrelations.equal_variables_note: The supplied quantifiers allow z=x. Requiring three distinct variables would discard the legitimate counterexample and is not authorized.
subrelations.restricted_carrier_note: On only segments centered at O this relation would be equality, but that special carrier is not stated and must not be invented.

property_evidence.reflexive: a intersect a is the entire line a and is nonempty.
property_evidence.symmetric: a intersect b equals b intersect a.
property_evidence.transitive: a:y=0, b:x=0, c:y=1: adjacent intersections are (0,0) and (0,1), but a intersect c is empty.

source_reviews.task: Determine whether parallelism according to the student's literal coplanar-and-disjoint definition is an equivalence relation.
source_reviews.carrier: Euclidean lines in a fixed plane, or all Euclidean three-space lines with coplanarity required by the relation.
source_reviews.relation: aRb iff a and b are coplanar AND their intersection is empty.
source_reviews.independent_solution: A line shares all its points with itself, so the no-common-point condition refutes reflexivity. Coplanarity and empty intersection are symmetric. For a:y=0, b:y=1, c=a, both adjacent relations hold but aRc is aRa and fails; repeated variables are allowed. Thus transitivity also fails. This literal relation is not an equivalence relation.

property_evidence.reflexive: a:y=0 is coplanar with itself but has infinitely many common points with itself, so not aRa.
property_evidence.symmetric: Swapping two coplanar disjoint lines preserves both requirements.
property_evidence.transitive: a:y=0 and b:y=1 in one plane satisfy aRb and bRa. With c=a, the conclusion aRa is false.

positive_example.limitation: A successful distinct-line chain does not prove transitivity for every triple and does not invalidate the c=a counterexample.

source_reviews.no_source_repair: Do not add coincidence-inclusive parallelism or a distinct-variable restriction to the quoted definition.
